chunks: I said: May I be your ransom! This is not our recitation. So what is the Messenger (Rasool), the Prophet (Nabi), and the Muhaddath?

He said: The Rasool is one to whom the Angel appears and speaks to him. The Nabi is one who sees in his dream; and sometimes Prophethood and Messengership are combined in one person. The Muhaddath is one who hears the voice but does not see the form.

He (the narrator) said: I said, May Allah keep you well! How does he know that what he saw in his dream is true and that it is from the Angel? He said: He is guided to it until he recognizes it. Verily Allah has sealed the Books with your Book and sealed the Prophets with your Prophet.

key_terms.الرسول: Rasool: A messenger who receives revelation through direct angelic visitation and speech
key_terms.المحدَّث: Muhaddath: One who hears the voice of the angel without seeing its form — a term applied to the Imams in Shia theology
key_terms.النبي: Nabi: A prophet who receives revelation through true dreams
key_terms.خاتم الأنبياء: Seal of the Prophets — Quranic title (33:40) applied to Prophet Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Rasool, Nabi, and Muhaddath in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this important dialogue, a companion asks Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to clarify the distinctions between three levels of divine communication: the Rasool (Messenger) who sees and speaks with the Angel, the Nabi (Prophet) who receives revelation through dreams, and the Muhaddath who hears the divine voice without seeing the form. This hadith addresses a key theological question about the hierarchy of prophetic roles and the nature of revelation (wahy). The Imam concludes by affirming the finality of prophethood with the Prophet Muhammad and the finality of scriptures with the Quran, providing the doctrinal basis for understanding the Imams as Muhaddathun — those who receive divine guidance through hearing without being prophets.
